key_insight: Translation-invariant topological CSS codes decouple into stacks of higher-form toric codes exactly when superlattice translations act trivially on every excitation layer and interlayer gluing vanishes.
engineering_relevance: This criterion and an explicit circuit-construction algorithm provide a systematic route to toric-code decompositions relevant to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Organize excitations into superselection layers and identify translation action and interlayer gluing.
For prime-p codes with finitely many excitation types per layer, remove gluing by further coarse-graining each direction by p^(m−1), once translations act trivially on all m nonzero layers.
Construct finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford decoupling circuits using SUM and SWAP gates, potentially with ancillas.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact theoretical criterion, a coarse-graining guarantee, and a constructive algorithm, but no numerical benchmarks or hardware evaluation.
watch_item: Coarse-graining by p^(m−1) can enlarge the unit cell substantially; practical circuit and ancilla costs are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
